The sigit.si command line interface.

Usage: si [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  auth     Sign in, sign out, and inspect your session
  me       Your sigit.si profile
  repo     List, create, and inspect repositories
  pr       List, open, and comment on pull requests
  issue    List, open, and comment on issues
  code     Read files and search code in a repository
  run      Start and follow siGit Code Cloud Agent runs
  site     Publish a repository's default branch as a static site
  status   Report and read commit statuses, the checks CI shows on a commit
  hook     Manage a repository's deploy webhooks
  session  Manage siGit Code Cloud Sessions
  billing  Plan, usage, and the hosted billing portal
  models   List the models a session can use
  browse   Open something on sigit.si in your browser
  api      Call the sigit.si API directly. The escape hatch for anything without a dedicated command
  mcp      Serve these commands to an AI agent as MCP tools over stdio
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -e, --environment <ENVIRONMENT>  Which sigit.si deployment to talk to. Overridden by SIGIT_HOST [env: SIGIT_ENVIRONMENT=] [default: production]
      --json                       Print machine-readable JSON instead of formatted text, where supported
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version

Sign in, sign out, and inspect your session

  login           Sign in with your sigit.si email and password
  logout          Sign out and remove the stored token
  status          Show who is currently signed in
  signup          Create a sigit.si account. A confirmation email follows
  resend          Send the confirmation email again
  reset-password  Email instructions for choosing a new password
  delete-account  Permanently delete your account
  setup-git       Let git use your sigit.si sign-in for clones and fetches, by adding a credential helper to your global git config
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

  -e, --environment <ENVIRONMENT>  Which sigit.si deployment to talk to. Overridden by SIGIT_HOST [env: SIGIT_ENVIRONMENT=] [default: production]

      --json                       Print machine-readable JSON instead of formatted text, where supported
